chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not eat upon a table upon which wine is drunk.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating at a table where wine is drunk according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a direct link between core theological conviction (Iman) and social etiquette, emphasizing that true faith necessitates avoiding the context of intoxication, not just the substance itself. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted as a preventive measure (sadd al-dhara'i) to maintain spiritual purity and social distinction from those prone to excess. The ruling highlights the Prophet's emphasis on the environment of consumption as a determinant of a believer's moral standing.
